title: The lighthouse keeper's lamp
text:
Far out on the rocky coast stood a tall white lighthouse. Its keeper was a quiet woman called Ibu Sari, and every evening she climbed the one hundred and twelve steps to light the great lamp at the top.

Her grandson, Dani, was staying for the holidays. He thought the lighthouse was boring. "Why do you do this every night?" he asked, panting at the top of the stairs. "Nobody ever looks at it."

Ibu Sari did not answer. She polished the glass until it shone and then pressed a switch. A beam of golden light swept out across the dark water.

That night, the wind began to howl. By midnight, grey clouds had swallowed the stars, and rain hammered the windows. Dani lay awake in his bed, listening to the waves crash against the rocks.

Suddenly, Ibu Sari shook his shoulder. "Quick, Dani. Come up with me." Together they hurried up the steps. Through the rain, far out at sea, Dani saw a tiny blinking light. It was a fishing boat, tossed about by the waves.

"They are lost," whispered Ibu Sari. "They cannot see the rocks. Our lamp must be their guide." She wiped the glass again and again so that the beam stayed bright and clear. Dani held the torch and watched the little boat. Slowly, very slowly, it turned and crept towards the harbour, keeping safely away from the rocks.

At dawn, three tired fishermen climbed up the steps to thank them. Their leader took off his hat. "Without your light, we would not be here," he said.

Dani looked at his grandmother's rough, steady hands. "I used to think this was a boring job," he said quietly. "Now I know it is the most important job in the world."
